In test/lisp/progmodes/python-tests.el (lines 35-45, 7656-7683), the unchanged test asserts (should-error (let ((debug-on-error nil)) (python-nav-end-of-statement))) expecting a legacy cl-assert or error on nominally overlapping triple-quoted strings, while its own FIXME notes that string syntax handling changed and the form now neither signals an error nor loops: python-syntax-stringify in lisp/progmodes/python.el (lines 961-964, 975-1022) places '|' string-fence properties on positions 3..4 and 7..8 rather than 8..9 (making remove-text-properties 8 9 a no-op), and python-nav-end-of-statement (lines 2358-2405; helpers at lines 580-593, 2557-2564, 6556-6568) contains no cl-assert, signal, or error form, guards out-of-order string-start with (when (>= string-start last-string-end) ...), catches scan-error, and unconditionally returns (point-marker) before with-temp-buffer teardown, so should-error deterministically fails its obsolete error premise while the normal failed outcome is preserved. The :unstable tag does not justify this category, and this source rule makes no claim about pre-teardown marker coordinates.

In test/lisp/gnus/message-tests.el (lines 111-142), the unchanged test gates execution with 1-argument (skip-unless (epg-check-configuration (epg-find-configuration 'OpenPGP))), omitting &optional req-versions so req-versions defaults to nil. In lisp/epg-config.el (lines 116-189, 260-280), whereas epg-find-configuration validates an installed GPG executable via 2-argument (epg-check-configuration configuration (cdr program-version)), a 1-argument call to epg-check-configuration with req-versions=nil evaluates (if (listp req-versions) req-versions (list req-versions)) to nil because (listp nil) is t; pcase-dolist therefore executes zero iterations, never reaches (or min epg-gpg-minimum-version) or (throw 'version-ok t), and unconditionally signals (error "Unsupported version: %s" version) (or (error "Undetermined version: %S" version) when version is not a string). skip-unless catches that unconditional error into an unreachable ert-test-skipped result regardless of GPG availability (this does not indicate GPG is uninstalled), while the original skipped outcome is preserved intact.
